_comment: G.3. The order the Arm C plus E.2 build happens in, written on
2026-08-31, before any of it has been attempted.
This is not frozen by hash the way G2_CRITERIA.json and
PREREGISTRATION.json are, and the difference is deliberate. Those two
are commitments: changing them after the fact would change what the
result means. A runbook is a plan, and a plan that cannot be revised
when a step turns out to be wrong is just a way of being wrong on
schedule. What is checked here is that the plan is complete and
consistent with the artefacts that already exist, not that it never
Every step names what it reads, what it writes, what makes you stop,
and whether it can be undone. chip/g3_runbook.py checks the lot.
budget_source: PLAN_TO_DECEMBER.md, G.3 row: 3-5 d plus machine time

raw_carried_forward.macro_lef: Arm B's hardened macro. The point of Arm B is that its geometry is fixed, so this file is an input to the build and not an output of it. If it ever changes, Arm B is a different arm and the two-arm result does not carry over.
raw_carried_forward.cost: chip/ARMC_COST.json, which armc_cost.py produces and gen_armc.py reads. It is an artefact of this phase rather than a build output, and it is already in the list the re-run regenerates.

steps.title: freeze the two-arm build before anything touches it
steps.stop: any raw input hashes differently from what chip/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json recorded, which means the build on disk is not the build the numbers came from

steps.title: put the generated modules into dualarm/src/ under their real names, then resync the top-level copy
steps.stop: chip/RTL_LINT.json does not report the drafts installable, or a destination in dualarm/src/ differs from the archived copy in any way the generators do not account for, which means somebody edited it by hand since 7 August

steps.title: source_files and pinout, by hand and reviewed
steps.stop: the tile count or the top module name would have to change, which is a different shuttle submission and not this build

steps.title: lint the installed RTL before spending machine time on it
steps.stop: any lint error, and any width warning on the arm decode, which is the expression the RTL notes as the one a synthesiser can widen unexpectedly

steps.title: the existing gate-level tests still pass
steps.stop: any test that passed on the two-arm build fails here, because that is a regression in arms A and B and they are the published result

steps.title: work the acceptance table row by row
steps.stop: any acceptance test fails, including the window that is only there to prove the sticky overflow flag sets

steps.title: pin Arm A and bind the sixteen Arm C regions
steps.stop: any place_cell is rejected, or any Arm A instance ends up at coordinates other than the ones it holds in the two-arm build

steps.title: the OpenLane run to GDS
steps.stop: DRC, LVS, antenna or timing is not clean, or the run needs a fifth tile, which G.2 already decided against and which would make the whole area argument moot

steps.title: XOR the new GDS against the frozen one
steps.stop: any geometry difference inside the area arms A and B occupy, because the two-arm result is quoted off that geometry and a moved wire there changes it

steps.title: pull the DEF, netlist, SPEF and positions back out
steps.stop: extraction exits non-zero, or the SPEF is missing nets the netlist has, which is the failure that makes every parasitic number quietly optimistic

steps.title: the whole evidence gate, against the three-arm build

expected_failures.why: the raw inputs are a different build now, so the recorded hashes are supposed to have moved. This is the one failure in the run that means the build worked.

steps.stop: any check fails that passed on the two-arm build and the reason is not written down in the same sitting, because a check that starts failing and gets explained a week later is a check nobody trusts

steps.title: re-cut the manifest against the build that now exists
steps.stop: an artefact hash moved and nothing in the run explains why, which means something is being regenerated from an input nobody is tracking
